title: How Zero Trust Branch Airgap+ micro-subnets work: address layout, DHCP server requirement, VLAN fields and CSV import

prose.text: {{airgap-plus-purdue}} {{mask-range-reserved}} The three protection solutions are compared in [[zero-trust-branch.operations.segmentation]].

prose.label: Configuring a VLAN.
prose.text: {{vlan-airgap-plus-fields}} {{range-overlap}} {{suitability}} {{csv-import-ips}} The wider operations area is in [[zero-trust-branch.operations]].

airgap-plus-purdue.statement: Some Purdue Level 2 and below endpoints require direct L2 connectivity, and Zero Trust Branch identifies and whitelists such endpoints in a special group called Airgap+ and continuously monitors them.

quotes: Some Purdue Level 2 and below endpoints require direct L2 connectivity (e.g., PLC controller to PLC controller).
Zero Trust Branch identifies and whitelists such endpoints in a special group called Airgap+, and continuously monitors those endpoints.

mask-range-reserved.statement: Micro-subnets support masks /27 through /30 and reserve three addresses (network, gateway, broadcast); a /29 gives 8 addresses with 5 left for endpoints.

quotes: Supports subnet masks /27 through /30, ensuring granular logical segmentation.
The micro-subnet has three reserved IP addresses.

a /29 subnet creates a segment of 8 IP addresses. Out of these 8 IP addresses, the first IP address is reserved for the network address, the second is reserved for the gateway, and the last is reserved for the broadcast address, leaving 5 IP addresses for endpoints

dhcp-server-only.statement: Airgap+ is supported only in DHCP server mode, and uses the Zero Trust Branch DHCP server because the micro-subnet allocation must be known to the server.

quotes: Airgap+ is supported only in DHCP server mode.
Airgap+ uses the Zero Trust Branch DHCP server, as the micro-subnet allocation must be known to the server.

boundary-enforcement.statement: Devices in the same micro-subnet communicate directly, and any micro-subnet-to-micro-subnet or external traffic is always routed through the appliance.

quotes: Direct Intra-Micro-Subnet Communication: Devices within the same micro-subnet interact without routing overhead.
Any micro-subnet-to-micro-subnet or external traffic is always routed through the appliance.

vlan-airgap-plus-fields.statement: Enabling Airgap+ on a VLAN takes a Netmask, an Airgap+ Range Start (the network address of the first micro-subnet) and an Airgap+ Range End (the broadcast address of the last micro-subnet).

quotes: Netmask: Select the subnet mask that must be used to determine the network scope for the asset in Airgap+ mode.
Airgap+ Range Start: Enter the network address of the first micro-subnet.
Airgap+ Range End: Enter the broadcast address of the last micro-subnet.

range-overlap.statement: The Airgap range cannot overlap with Airgap+; in the page's example 10.90.10.8 to 10.90.10.23 defines the /29 micro-subnets, and 10.90.10.x/24 endpoints outside the Airgap+ range are assigned /32 addresses.

quotes: the Airgap range cannot overlap with Airgap+. For example, 10.90.10.8 to 10.90.10.23 defines the range for /29 micro-subnets. 10.90.10.x/24 endpoints outside Airgap+ range are assigned with /32 IP addresses.

suitability.statement: Airgap+ suits deployments where some endpoints cannot get a /32 mask and the device IP address is flexible enough to fit the available micro-subnets; if the IP address is not flexible, Airgap-Lite is used by changing the protection at the asset level; the page's own asset-edit steps instead select Network from a Segmentation Granularity drop-down menu.

quotes: Some endpoints cannot get a /32 mask.
The device IP address is flexible, because it must fit into the microsegments available for endpoints defined by the Airgap+ configuration.
If the device IP address is not flexible, use Airgap-Lite by changing the security protection at the asset level.
Select Network from the Segmentation Granularity drop-down menu.

csv-import-ips.statement: In the page's example, the IP addresses of the Airgap+ endpoints vlan10-dev3 and vlan10-dev4 are used from the CSV file, while for vlan10-dev1 and vlan10-dev2, which are not part of the micro-subnet, the IP address field is empty and the /32 IP address is assigned by the DHCP server.

quotes: the IP addresses for the Airgap+ endpoints (vlan10-dev3 and vlan10-dev4) are used from the CSV file
For the endpoints that are not part of the micro-subnet (vlan10-dev1 and vlan10-dev2), the IP address field is empty and the /32 IP address is assigned by the DHCP server.
